When the model generates a response, it may draw on spans that are irrelevant to the query and produce a confident, coherent answer grounded in the wrong part of the context. This paper argues that such failures constitute a distinct phenomenon, which we call Ghost Context, and that the existing taxonomy of hallucination does not adequately capture them. A hallucinating model invents information that is absent from context. A model exhibiting Ghost Context uses information that is present but should not influence the current output. The error is not fabrication; it is misattribution. Critically, Ghost Context can occur even when every span in the context is individually authorized for the user and permissible for the application, making it difficult to detect for access control mechanisms and standard faithfulness checks that treat the context as an undifferentiated pool of evidence. We formalize Ghost Context, propose a taxonomy of four interference patterns, describe a mask-and-rerun detection methodology, and outline the security implications for retrieval-augmented generation and agent memory systems. We argue that reliable deployment of long-context models requires distinguishing Ghost Context from conventional hallucination and developing targeted mitigation strategies for cross-context interference.<\/jats:p>","DOI":"10.36227\/techrxiv.177162116.61215374\/v1","type":"posted-content","created":{"date-parts":[[2026,2,20]],"date-time":"2026-02-20T20:59:27Z","timestamp":1771621167000},"source":"Crossref","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["Ghost Context: Cross-Context Hallucination in Long-Context Language Models"],"prefix":"10.36227","author":[{"ORCID":"https:\/\/orcid.org\/0009-0003-8516-0723","authenticated-orcid":false,"given":"Rohith","family":"Namboothiri","sequence":"first","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]}],"member":"263","link":[{"URL":"https:\/\/www.techrxiv.org\/doi\/pdf\/10.36227\/techrxiv.177162116.61215374\/v1","content-type":"unspecified","content-version":"vor","intended-application":"similarity-checking"}],"deposited":{"date-parts":[[2026,6,12]],"date-time":"2026-06-12T15:50:53Z","timestamp":1781279453000},"score":45.19693,"resource":{"primary":{"URL":"https:\/\/www.techrxiv.org\/doi\/full\/10.36227\/techrxiv.177162116.61215374\/v1"}},"issued":{"date-parts":[[2026,2,20]]},"references-count":0,"URL":"https:\/\/doi.org\/10.36227\/techrxiv.177162116.61215374\/v1","published":{"date-parts":[[2026,2,20]]},"subtype":"preprint"},{"indexed":{"date-parts":[[2025,6,3]],"date-time":"2025-06-03T04:01:21Z","timestamp":1748923281851,"version":"3.41.0"},"reference-count":0,"publisher":"Everant Journals","issue":"05","content-domain":{"domain":[],"crossmark-restriction":false},"short-container-title":["IJMEI"],"abstract":"This study analyzes the determinants of the trade-off between rating-based assessment and the requirement for real collateral in bank lending to Moroccan SMEs, particularly in a context of deteriorating balance sheet fundamentals. Facing post-pandemic economic challenges and rising non-performing loans, Moroccan banking institutions are confronted with a major dilemma: strengthen their dependence on internal rating systems or favor tangible guarantees. Our research, based on a sample of 237 SMEs and covering the period 2019-2024, demonstrates that the deterioration of SMEs' financial indicators leads to a significant shift in the balance in favor of real guarantees, to the detriment of the rating approach. This evolution, while securing the banking system in the short term, risks exacerbating inequalities in access to financing and hindering the recovery of the Moroccan entrepreneurial fabric. Practical recommendations and policy perspectives are proposed to rebalance this A full characterization of memory must include how participants use exogenous and endogenous cues to guide retrieval. In free recall, in which endogenous cues play a large role, retrieved context theories have emerged as a leading explanation of data on the dynamics of memory search (Lohnas & Healey, 2021). More recently, Logan and colleagues have advanced a retrieved context model to explain data on serial recall and motor production (Logan, 2021; Logan & Cox, 2021; Logan, 2018; Logan & Cox, 2023). Comparisons of recall transitions have further highlighted similarities among these tasks (e.g., Bhatarah et al., 2008; Golomb et al., 2008). Here I evaluate retrieved context theory\u2019s ability to simultaneously account for data from these classic recall procedures. I show how a serial version of the context maintenance and retrieval model (termed sCMR) can account for dissociations between serial position curves and temporal clustering effects. I also show how sCMR can account for grouping effects in serial recall, extending the assumptions of grouping from free recall (Lohnas et al., 2023). The sCMR model provides a common theoretical framework to harmonize the disparate phenomena studied using these classic memory procedures, but also reveals the distinctions between serial and free recall through their relative dependence on different model-based mechanisms.<\/p>","DOI":"10.31234\/osf.io\/9t4y6","type":"posted-content","created":{"date-parts":[[2024,1,1]],"date-time":"2024-01-01T05:00:27Z","timestamp":1704085227000},"source":"Crossref","is-referenced-by-count":1,"title":["A retrieved context model of serial recall and free recall"],"prefix":"10.31234","author":[{"ORCID":"https:\/\/orcid.org\/0000-0002-1204-8760","authenticated-orcid":true,"given":"Lynn J.","family":"Lohnas","sequence":"first","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]}],"member":"15934","deposited":{"date-parts":[[2024,2,5]],"date-time":"2024-02-05T19:51:40Z","timestamp":1707162700000},"score":41.732,"resource":{"primary":{"URL":"https:\/\/osf.io\/9t4y6"}},"issued":{"date-parts":[[2023,12,31]]},"references-count":0,"URL":"https:\/\/doi.org\/10.31234\/osf.io\/9t4y6","published":{"date-parts":[[2023,12,31]]},"subtype":"preprint"},{"indexed":{"date-parts":[[2025,5,20]],"date-time":"2025-05-20T04:10:16Z","timestamp":1747714216214,"version":"3.40.5"},"posted":{"date-parts":[[2023,12,31]]},"group-title":"PsyArXiv","reference-count":0,"publisher":"Center for Open Science","license":[{"start":{"date-parts":[[2023,12,31]],"date-time":"2023-12-31T00:00:00Z","timestamp":1703980800000},"content-version":"unspecified","delay-in-days":0,"URL":"https:\/\/creativecommons.org\/licenses\/by\/4.0\/legalcode"}],"content-domain":{"domain":[],"crossmark-restriction":false},"abstract":"
